catalogue: Australian residential roof drainage and overflow components

ncc_references.relationship: Roof drainage context. Catchment, rainfall intensity, hydraulic sizing, overflow paths, discharge and project limitations must be checked for the actual site.

objects.name: roof drainage system
objects.definition: The above-ground assembly that collects water from roof catchments, carries it through gutters and outlets, provides safe overflow paths, and delivers it to a downpipe, tank inlet or underground stormwater system.
functions: Collect runoff from roof catchments
Convey design flows without damaging the building
Provide visible or controlled overflow when normal outlets cannot accept the flow

cad.pattern: Connected collection runs, outlets, vertical leaders and overflow paths around each roof catchment
cad.placement: At roof drainage edges and low points, continuing down the building to stormwater discharge
cad.start: Roof catchment discharge edge or low point
cad.end: Underground drain, tank inlet or approved discharge
cad.opening: Outlets and overflow openings interrupt gutter walls

notes: The ontology identifies physical parts; it does not calculate hydraulic capacity or approve a discharge point.

objects.name: eaves gutter system
objects.definition: A roof-edge drainage assembly comprising an eaves gutter, supports, stop ends, corners and joins where needed, one or more outlets, and the specified continuous or dedicated overflow measures.
functions: Collect water leaving the lower roof edge
Carry water to gutter outlets
Keep overflow from entering or damaging the building

cad.pattern: Continuous gutter run along an eaves line, broken by corners, stop ends, outlets and expansion details
cad.placement: Outside the building at the lower roof edge
cad.start: Stop end, corner or high point
cad.end: Stop end, corner or expansion detail
cad.opening: Has outlet and designed overflow openings

objects.name: box gutter system
objects.definition: An internal or concealed roof drainage assembly in which a box-section gutter collects water between or beside roof areas and discharges through a sized outlet or sump with an independent overflow path.
functions: Collect runoff at an internal roof low line
Carry water to a sump or outlet
Provide an overflow route that protects the building if the normal outlet is restricted

cad.pattern: Continuous formed channel falling to a sump or outlet with a separately modelled overflow path
cad.placement: Within the roof footprint between roof planes or behind a parapet
cad.start: Closed high end or catchment boundary
cad.opening: Has normal discharge and independent overflow openings

notes: Box gutters are not covered by the simple eaves-gutter construction path in Housing Provisions 7.4.3; the AS/NZS 3500.3 pathway must be checked.

objects.name: eaves gutter overflow system
objects.definition: The deliberate set of openings, lowered edges, spacers or dedicated devices that lets excess water escape an eaves gutter outward before it can enter or damage the building.
functions: Release excess water when normal outlets are exceeded or blocked
Direct overflow visibly away from the building
Preserve a continuous overflow path along or at nominated parts of the gutter

cad.pattern: Continuous gap or repeated slots, or one or more dedicated devices sized to the gutter run
cad.placement: At the outward face, rear gap or stop end of an eaves gutter
cad.start: Beginning of the designed overflow provision
cad.end: End of the designed overflow provision
cad.opening: Is itself an open escape path through or around the gutter

notes: A high-front gutter needs a clear, intentional overflow measure; a visually plausible profile is not enough.

objects.name: roof gutter
objects.definition: A long open channel at a roof edge or low line that intercepts runoff and conveys it to an outlet.
functions: Collect roof runoff
Carry water to outlets
Form part of a controlled drainage and overflow system

cad.pattern: Continuous open channel with repeated supports and discrete outlets
cad.placement: At a roof drainage edge or low line
cad.start: Stop end, corner or high point
cad.end: Stop end, corner or outlet transition
cad.opening: Open along its top and interrupted by outlets and overflow devices

objects.name: eaves gutter
objects.definition: An external gutter fixed along the lower edge of a roof to receive runoff discharged over the eaves end of the roof covering.
functions: Catch water at the eaves
Convey water to downpipe outlets
Overflow outward through the selected overflow measure

cad.pattern: Continuous profile along the eaves with joints, corners, brackets and outlets
cad.placement: Immediately below the roof covering discharge edge
cad.opening: Receives water through its open top and discharges through outlet and overflow openings

objects.name: box gutter
objects.definition: A generally rectangular, internally located gutter with a defined sole, sides, depth and fall, forming the main channel of a box gutter system.
functions: Collect water between internal roof boundaries
Carry water to a sump or outlet
Contain design flow while maintaining required freeboard and overflow

cad.pattern: Continuous rectangular channel falling to a discharge point
cad.placement: Within the roof footprint or behind a parapet
cad.opening: Open above and connected to normal and overflow discharge paths

objects.name: valley gutter
objects.definition: A formed open channel running down the internal angle where two roof planes meet, receiving water from both sides and carrying it toward the eaves or another collector.
functions: Weather the junction between converging roof planes
Collect runoff from both roof planes
Carry valley flow to the lower drainage system

cad.pattern: Single sloping channel following each internal roof intersection
cad.placement: Under the cut edges of coverings on both sides of a roof valley
cad.end: Eaves gutter, rainhead or lower roof drainage transition
cad.opening: Open along the valley with covering clearances at both sides

notes: Valley gutter and valley flashing are often used loosely for the same visible piece; retain both search terms but classify the physical piece by its water-carrying role.

objects.name: soaker gutter
objects.definition: A narrow concealed or partly concealed channel that receives water beside a roof abutment or beneath covering edges and conveys it to a lower gutter or roof surface.
functions: Collect water at a difficult roof abutment
Provide a concealed drainage route under adjacent covering
Discharge collected water to a visible lower drainage surface

cad.pattern: Narrow channel along an abutment or beneath a covering edge
cad.placement: At a roof-wall or roof-covering junction requiring a concealed drainage path
cad.opening: Open or lapped beneath the adjacent covering

notes: Terminology overlaps with soaker tray and individual soakers; select the object from its continuous channel geometry and discharge role.

objects.name: gutter stop end
objects.definition: A closed fitting sealed to the end of a gutter profile to retain normal flow, sometimes shaped or lowered to act as a dedicated overflow weir.
functions: Close the end of a gutter run
Contain water within the gutter profile
Provide an overflow crest when specifically configured as a weir
not_synonyms: end-stop weir unless lowered or opened

cad.pattern: One component at each closed gutter end
cad.placement: Across the open section at the end of a gutter
cad.opening: Normally none; may include a designed overflow opening or lowered crest

objects.name: internal gutter corner
objects.definition: A gutter fitting that joins two eaves gutter runs around a concave plan corner while maintaining a continuous water path.
functions: Turn an eaves gutter through an internal plan corner
Join matching gutter profiles
Maintain water containment and overflow continuity

cad.pattern: One fitting at each concave eaves plan corner
cad.placement: Between two eaves gutter runs
cad.opening: Open above to receive water

objects.name: external gutter corner
objects.definition: A gutter fitting that joins two eaves gutter runs around a convex plan corner while maintaining a continuous water path.
functions: Turn an eaves gutter around an external plan corner
Join matching gutter profiles
Maintain water containment and overflow continuity

cad.pattern: One fitting at each convex eaves plan corner
cad.placement: Between two eaves gutter runs
cad.opening: Open above to receive water

objects.name: gutter joiner
objects.definition: A sleeve, union or shaped connector that aligns and seals the ends of two compatible gutter lengths while allowing the specified joint behaviour.
functions: Connect adjacent gutter lengths
Maintain profile alignment
Seal the joint while accommodating system-specific movement

cad.pattern: Discrete connectors between stock or movement-limited gutter lengths
cad.placement: Around aligned gutter ends
cad.opening: Continues the open gutter channel

objects.name: gutter expansion joint
objects.definition: A deliberately detailed gutter joint that permits thermal movement between gutter lengths without losing the designed water path or overflow behaviour.
functions: Accommodate gutter thermal movement
Separate long gutter runs into movement lengths
Maintain water containment across the movement detail
materials: formed metal or proprietary compatible components

cad.pattern: Discrete movement details at designed intervals along long gutter runs
cad.placement: Across a gutter run with independent support to both sides as detailed
cad.opening: Continues the hydraulic channel while permitting movement

objects.name: gutter bracket
objects.definition: A repeated support fixed to fascia, rafter ends or another designed substrate to hold an eaves gutter at its required line and fall.
functions: Support the gutter and contained water
Maintain gutter line, level and fall
Resist outward, downward and wind actions on the gutter

cad.pattern: Repeated components at scheduled centres and near ends, corners and outlets
cad.placement: Between the gutter and its fascia or structural support
cad.opening: May create part of a controlled back gap when designed for that purpose

objects.name: gutter spacer
objects.definition: A purpose-selected block, spacer or bracket feature that holds an eaves gutter away from the fascia to create and preserve a controlled rear overflow gap.
functions: Set a consistent gap behind the gutter
Keep the rear overflow path unobstructed
Transfer gutter support through the designed bracket or fixing arrangement

cad.pattern: Repeated stand-offs along the rear of the gutter
cad.placement: Between gutter support and fascia where a rear overflow gap is selected
cad.opening: Defines rather than fills the rear overflow opening

objects.name: gutter outlet
objects.definition: A formed fitting through the sole, face or end of a gutter that transfers normal drainage flow into a downpipe, rainhead or other receiving component.
functions: Open a controlled discharge from the gutter
Connect gutter flow to the next drainage component
Provide the designed hydraulic throat without obstructing the gutter

cad.pattern: One or more discrete outlets at gutter low points or designed positions
cad.placement: Through the gutter sole, face or stop end
cad.opening: Requires a cut opening in the gutter

notes: Dropper, pop and nozzle vary by region and product; store them as search terms and retain gutter outlet as the neutral object name.

objects.name: gutter back outlet
objects.definition: A gutter outlet passing through the rear wall of an eaves gutter into a rainhead or offset connection rather than dropping directly through the gutter sole.
functions: Discharge gutter water through the back face
Connect an eaves gutter to a rainhead or offset inlet
Avoid a direct bottom drop where the detailed system requires a rear connection

cad.pattern: Discrete rear outlet at a nominated gutter discharge point
cad.placement: Through the back face of an eaves gutter
cad.opening: Requires a formed opening through the gutter rear wall

objects.name: box gutter sump
objects.definition: A depressed collection box at the discharge end or low point of a box gutter, providing a larger hydraulic transition to the outlet and normally coordinating with an overflow path.
functions: Collect water from the box gutter
Provide head and space around the normal outlet
Coordinate normal discharge and independent overflow

cad.pattern: Discrete depressed box at a box gutter discharge point
cad.placement: Below the sole of a box gutter at a designed low point
cad.start: Box gutter end or side entry
cad.opening: Open to the gutter and penetrated by normal and overflow discharge openings

objects.name: rainhead
objects.definition: An external, open-topped or visibly overflowing collection box that receives water from a gutter or roof outlet and feeds a downpipe while providing separation and overflow capacity.
functions: Receive discharge from a gutter or roof outlet
Feed a connected downpipe
Make surcharge or overflow visible and direct it away from the wall

cad.pattern: Discrete external collection heads at gutter or box-gutter discharge points
cad.placement: Outside the wall below or beside the incoming gutter outlet
cad.opening: Open at top or face and includes a visible overflow path

notes: A rainhead is external and visibly relieves surcharge; do not substitute it automatically for an internal box-gutter sump.

objects.name: downpipe
objects.definition: A primarily vertical pipe that carries roof water from a gutter outlet, rainhead or sump to an underground stormwater drain, tank inlet, spreader or approved discharge point.
functions: Convey roof water down the building
Connect roof outlets to the site stormwater system
Keep discharge controlled and clear of the building fabric

cad.pattern: Vertical runs with discrete bends, offsets, clips, joins and lower connections
cad.placement: On or near an external wall below each roof drainage outlet
cad.end: Underground stormwater drain, tank, spreader or approved discharge
cad.opening: Connects through outlet, tank or drain sockets but is otherwise closed

objects.name: round downpipe
objects.definition: A downpipe with a circular cross-section, assembled from compatible round pipe lengths, sockets or joiners, bends, clips and lower connection fittings.
functions: Convey roof water vertically
Provide a circular hydraulic section
Connect to matching round fittings and stormwater adaptors

cad.pattern: Circular pipe route following the scheduled downpipe path
cad.placement: Below a roof drainage outlet
cad.opening: Open only at connected ends

objects.name: rectangular downpipe
objects.definition: A downpipe with a rectangular or near-rectangular cross-section, assembled from matching pipe lengths, bends, offsets, clips and lower connection fittings.
functions: Convey roof water vertically
Provide a compact flat-sided external profile
Connect to matching rectangular fittings

cad.pattern: Rectangular pipe route following the scheduled downpipe path
cad.placement: Below a roof drainage outlet
cad.opening: Open only at connected ends

notes: Square downpipe is a useful search term, but a rectangular product is not necessarily square.

objects.name: downpipe bend
objects.definition: A shaped fitting that changes the direction of a downpipe run by a stated angle while maintaining a continuous internal waterway.
functions: Change downpipe direction
Form offsets and lower shoes with compatible fittings
Maintain a closed water path through the change

cad.pattern: Discrete directional fittings at each route change
cad.placement: Between aligned downpipe lengths
cad.opening: Open at both connected ends

objects.name: downpipe offset assembly
objects.definition: A short dog-leg in a downpipe made from two bends and an intermediate pipe length, used to shift the downpipe axis around an eaves projection or other obstruction.
functions: Shift the downpipe between non-aligned upper and lower axes
Clear the eaves, fascia or wall projection
Maintain continuous gravity flow through the route change

cad.pattern: Two bends separated by a sloping pipe segment
cad.placement: Between the gutter outlet and wall-aligned vertical downpipe, or around another obstruction
cad.opening: Open only at connected ends

objects.name: downpipe joiner
objects.definition: A socket, sleeve or formed connector that joins two downpipe lengths while preserving alignment and a continuous waterway.
functions: Connect downpipe lengths
Maintain cross-section alignment
Provide the required lap, socket or sealed joint

cad.pattern: Discrete connectors between downpipe stock lengths
cad.placement: Around the abutting or telescoped ends of downpipe lengths
cad.opening: Open at both connected ends

objects.name: downpipe clip
objects.definition: A repeated strap, saddle or proprietary bracket that holds a downpipe to a wall or frame while keeping its route, clearance and joints stable.
functions: Restrain the downpipe to its support
Maintain alignment and wall clearance
Transfer pipe, water and wind actions to the building

cad.pattern: Repeated clips at scheduled centres and near fittings
cad.placement: Around the downpipe and fixed to the supporting wall or frame
cad.opening: Wraps or saddles the pipe without opening its waterway

objects.name: downpipe shoe
objects.definition: A curved or angled open-ended fitting at the bottom of a downpipe that turns discharge away from the wall onto a lower roof, surface drain or approved open discharge location.
functions: Turn downpipe flow outward at its base
Direct open discharge away from the wall
Reduce uncontrolled wetting at the downpipe termination

cad.pattern: One open turn-out at a free-discharge downpipe termination
cad.placement: At the bottom of a downpipe above its receiving surface
cad.opening: Open at the outward end

objects.name: downpipe spreader
objects.definition: A horizontal distribution fitting at a downpipe outlet that divides or spreads discharge across a lower roof so the receiving roof covering and drainage system are not loaded at one small point.
functions: Distribute upper-roof water across a lower roof
Reduce concentrated discharge at one point
Direct flow down the receiving roof toward its drainage edge

cad.pattern: Short horizontal branch with repeated or opposed outlets
cad.placement: At a downpipe termination above a lower roof
cad.end: Distributed openings over the lower roof
cad.opening: Has multiple designed discharge openings

notes: The lower roof and its drainage system must be designed for the added upper-roof catchment; the object itself does not prove capacity.

objects.name: downpipe-to-stormwater adaptor
objects.definition: A transition fitting at ground level that connects the shape and size of an above-ground downpipe to the inlet of an underground stormwater drain or tank line.
functions: Transition between downpipe and stormwater pipe geometry
Provide a controlled lower connection
Keep the connection accessible or sealed as required by the selected system

cad.pattern: One transition at each connected downpipe base
cad.placement: At or just above ground over the underground drain inlet
cad.opening: Open at both connected ends

objects.name: front-face gutter overflow slot
objects.definition: One of a repeated series of purpose-formed openings through the outer face of an eaves gutter, positioned to release excess water outward below the level that could threaten the building.
functions: Provide continuous-distribution overflow capacity
Make gutter surcharge visible
Direct overflow through the front rather than behind the gutter
materials: opening in metal or uPVC gutter face

cad.pattern: Repeated openings along the outward gutter face
cad.placement: Through the front face of an eaves gutter
cad.opening: Is a cut or formed opening through the gutter face

objects.name: controlled gutter back gap
objects.definition: A continuous designed gap between the back of an eaves gutter and the fascia or building face, kept open by compatible spacers, clips or brackets so excess water can escape behind and below the gutter without entering the building.
functions: Provide a continuous rear overflow path
Prevent the gutter back from sealing against the fascia
Release surcharge below vulnerable building openings or edges
materials: air space defined by gutter supports and spacers

cad.pattern: Continuous linear void behind the gutter, interrupted only by compatible narrow supports
cad.placement: Between the gutter rear wall and fascia or building face
cad.opening: Is itself the designed open gap

notes: Model the gap as a required void; adding arbitrary packers or sealant can destroy the intended overflow path.

objects.name: controlled gutter front bead
objects.definition: A deliberately lowered or shaped outer gutter edge that establishes a continuous front overflow crest below the level at which water could flow into the building.
functions: Set the overflow crest on the gutter front
Provide continuous outward overflow
Prevent an excessively high front edge from trapping surcharge against the building
materials: formed metal or uPVC gutter edge

cad.pattern: Continuous lowered outer edge along the gutter run
cad.placement: At the outward top edge of an eaves gutter
cad.opening: Defines the open overflow crest above the front edge

objects.name: gutter end-stop overflow weir
objects.definition: A lowered, notched or purpose-opened portion of a gutter stop end that forms a dedicated overflow crest discharging visibly beyond the end of the gutter.
functions: Provide a dedicated end overflow
Set a known overflow crest
Direct surcharge clear of the building at a visible location

cad.pattern: One or more dedicated weirs at gutter ends
cad.placement: Through or over the outward part of a gutter stop end
cad.opening: Is a lowered or open section of the stop end

objects.name: inverted gutter overflow nozzle
objects.definition: A dedicated outward-projecting overflow fitting installed through the gutter face with its entry or geometry arranged to set the overflow level and discharge excess water visibly.
functions: Provide a dedicated overflow opening
Project overflow beyond the gutter face
Make surcharge visible at a nominated location

cad.pattern: Discrete projecting devices at designed gutter overflow points
cad.placement: Through the front or stop end of an eaves gutter
cad.opening: Requires a matched opening through the gutter

objects.name: gutter front-face overflow weir
objects.definition: A purpose-cut or formed broad opening in the front face of an eaves gutter, with a defined lower crest that releases excess water outward as a dedicated weir.
functions: Provide a broad dedicated overflow
Set a controlled overflow level
Release water visibly through the gutter front
materials: opening in metal or uPVC gutter face

cad.pattern: One or more broad openings in the outward gutter face
cad.placement: Through the front face of an eaves gutter
cad.opening: Is a dedicated cut or formed weir opening

objects.name: rainhead overflow opening
objects.definition: A visible opening, lowered edge or hole in a rainhead that releases surcharge before the incoming gutter or internal drainage path can back up into the building.
functions: Relieve rainhead surcharge
Provide visible evidence of restricted or exceeded normal drainage
Direct overflow away from the wall and openings
materials: opening in metal or uPVC rainhead

cad.pattern: One or more visible relief openings on each overflow rainhead
cad.placement: Through a rainhead face or as a lowered open edge
cad.opening: Is the designed surcharge relief opening

objects.name: gutter guard
objects.definition: A perforated, mesh or formed cover installed over a gutter or roof-to-gutter gap to reduce entry of leaves and larger debris while allowing water to enter the drainage system.
functions: Reduce large debris entering the gutter
Preserve water entry to the gutter
Support maintenance and bushfire or pest detailing where the selected system is suitable

cad.pattern: Continuous or modular porous cover along selected gutter runs
cad.placement: Over the gutter opening and sometimes up the adjacent roof covering
cad.opening: Porous surface admits water through repeated apertures

notes: Gutter guard changes water-entry, debris and maintenance behaviour and must not obstruct the designed overflow path.

objects.name: rainwater chain
objects.definition: An exposed chain or linked cup assembly that guides water downward from a gutter outlet to a receiving drain or basin as an open alternative to a closed downpipe in suitable locations.
functions: Guide roof water down an exposed path
Provide a visible architectural drainage element
Deliver water to a designed splash-controlled receiver

cad.pattern: Single exposed vertical line beneath a compatible gutter outlet
cad.placement: In open air between a roof outlet and splash-controlled receiver
cad.end: Basin, drain or approved surface receiver
cad.opening: Open drainage path along the full length

notes: Use only where open discharge, wind-driven splash, capacity, safety and the receiving surface are deliberately resolved.
